INSTRUMENT NOT BUILT. What it must do: for each rule the canon set states, establish that exactly one document states it and the others POINT. The tractable form is not "detect duplicated meaning" -- that is a read -- but a two-sided check on the rules that carry IDS: for every `IN-*` rule id, the document that OWNS it is the rule library, and a canon document mentioning that id must cite it rather than reproduce its text. THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS: plant a paraphrase of an owned rule in a canon document and the check must fire, because a checker that only catches VERBATIM copies passes the case that actually happens -- prose forks by rewording, not by duplication.
BUILT AND GREEN 2026-09-02: `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/canon_states_a_rule_once.rs`. Population DERIVED by walking the rule library -- 66 rules parsed, with a guard that a small population is treated as a parse failure rather than as a clean result. The check is a sliding 12-word window over each rule's own summary against each canon document; measured today, zero canon documents reproduce any rule's words, and the documents DO cite rule ids, which is asserted positively so that `points rather than copies` cannot be satisfied by saying nothing at all. Control driven both ways in one test: a document that merely CITES the id must NOT fire (otherwise the check fires on the behaviour the criterion asks for) and a document carrying the rule's words MUST fire.

THE NOTE ABOVE ASKED FOR A PARAPHRASE CONTROL AND THIS INSTRUMENT DOES NOT MEET IT. I said prose forks by rewording rather than by duplication, which is true, and a test cannot decide whether two differently-worded paragraphs state one rule -- that is a judgement about meaning, the kind AC-00.2 and AC-00.3 were minted NON-TEST for. SO A GREEN HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT NO RULE HAS TWO HOMES: it is evidence that none has two homes BY COPY-PASTE, which is the cheap half. The limit is stated at the top of the test file rather than left for a reader to discover, and raised with vc, because a test whose stated purpose exceeds its reach is the vacuous instrument wearing a criterion's name. If vc wants the paraphrase half covered it needs a non-test arm.
